Ingredients:
- 6 oz short pasta (shells, rotini, or orecchiette)
- 8 oz chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 large yellow onion, thinly sliced
- 2 Tbsp olive oil, divided
- 1 clove garlic, minced (optional)
- 1 tsp all-purpose flour
- 1 tsp bouillon paste or 1/2 cup chicken broth
- 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce (optional)
- 2 Tbsp heavy cream or milk (optional, for a creamier sauce)
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Fresh thyme or dried herbs, to taste (optional)
- Reserved pasta water, as needed

Equipment:
- Large pot for boiling pasta
- Heavy-bottomed skillet or stock pot
- Wooden spoon or spatula
- Colander
- Bowl (for resting the chicken)
- Knife and cutting board

Instructions:
1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add the pasta and cook until al dente. Reserve about 1 cup of pasta water, then drain and set aside.
2. Pat the chicken dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat 1 Tbsp olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high. Add the chicken and brown on all sides until cooked through, about 5–7 minutes. Remove to a bowl with a slotted spoon.

5. Stir in the cream (if using) and a splash of reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
6. Return the chicken to the skillet along with the drained pasta and thyme. Toss to coat, adding more pasta water a tablespoon at a time if it looks dry. Simmer 2–3 minutes, taste, and adjust salt and pepper.
7. Serve hot.

Storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave with a splash of water or broth to loosen the sauce. Not recommended for freezing once the cream is added, as the sauce may separate.

- 5 large eggs

- 1/2 tsp salt
- 5 tbsp (about 40 g) all-purpose flour
- 1 1/2 tsp baking powder
- Powdered sugar, for dusting (optional)

- Parchment paper

- Small saucepan (or microwave-safe bowl)
- Whisk

- Wire cooling rack

3. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar by hand for about 2 minutes, until well blended and beginning to thicken.
4. Sift the flour, salt, and baking powder over the egg mixture. Fold and stir gently with the whisk until just combined.
5. Gradually fold the chocolate mixture into the batter, about 1/4 cup at a time. Add it slowly so the warm chocolate doesn't cook the eggs.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
7. Bake for 35–40 minutes, until the center is set but still slightly moist and a toothpick comes out with a few crumbs attached.
8. Let the cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely. Dust with powdered sugar before serving, if desired.

**Title:** Flourless-Style Chocolate Cake (Easy on the Flour)

**Ingredients:**
- 10 oz (280 g) bittersweet or dark chocolate, coarsely chopped
- 1 cup (2 sticks / 225 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
- 5 large eggs
- 1 cup plus 5 Tbsp (245 g) granulated sugar
- ½ tsp salt
- 5 Tbsp all-purpose flour
- 1½ tsp baking powder
- Powdered sugar, for dusting (optional)

**Equipment:**
- 9-inch (23 cm) round cake pan or springform pan
- Parchment paper
- Large heatproof bowl
- Small saucepan (for a bain-marie) or microwave-safe bowl
- Whisk
- Sifter or fine-mesh strainer
- Rubber spatula
- Cooling rack

**Instructions:**
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease your cake pan and line the bottom with parchment paper.
2. Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water (or in short bursts in the microwave), stirring until smooth. Set aside to cool slightly.
3. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar by hand for about 2 minutes, until well blended and beginning to thicken.
4. Sift the flour, salt, and baking powder over the egg mixture and fold gently with the whisk until just combined.
5. Gradually fold the warm chocolate mixture into the batter, about ¼ cup at a time, stirring gently. Adding it slowly keeps the chocolate from cooking the eggs.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.
7. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until the cake is set at the edges but still slightly soft in the center. A toothpick inserted near the edge should come out with a few moist crumbs.
8. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely. Dust with powdered sugar before serving, if desired.

**Storage:**
Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerate for up to 5 days (bring to room temperature before serving for the best texture). It also freezes well, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months.
